chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Whoever dies on the road to Mecca, whether going or returning, is safe from the Great Terror on the Day of Resurrection."

key_terms.الْفَزَعِ الْأَكْبَرِ: The Great Terror/Awe (a specific eschatological event)
key_terms.طَرِيقِ مَكَّةَ: The road to Mecca (path of pilgrimage)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for dying during the journey to Mecca for pilgrimage?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the high status of the traveler in the state of *Ihram*, linking their death to the divine mercy that spares them the overwhelming fear of the Day of Resurrection. Scholars note that 'Al-Faza' al-Akbar' refers to the intense anxiety faced by all creation, making this a specific guarantee of peace for those who perish while fulfilling the pilgrimage duty. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the sanctity of the journey itself as an act of worship, where the path to the House of God confers spiritual protection.
